bandReviews.observations: Complete printed Klarinette in A, Allegro, clef, three-flat key signature and common time; all opening rests, poco f, initial slurred entry, dotted notes and final high triplet groups/3 numerals/upper arch are preserved.

Opening dotted figure and dim., low descending groups, all ledger lines and natural sign, full low p including descender, all lower ties/slurs, and the final sustained-note tie extending to the right edge are intact.

Opening low tied ledger note and four-note figure, both hairpins and natural signs, rests, full pp under the high four-note entry, highest ledger note and arch, later low slurred figure and final rest match the original.

First two rest bars and subsequent f entry are complete; both triplet numerals and highest note/arch, dotted/slurred following notes, articulated group, and final low-to-high beamed figure are intact. Neighboring cello slur and high note fragments remain at the lower boundary.

All repeated dotted and high ledger-note figures are present, including naturals, final chromatic run with every sharp/natural, and both lower/upper slurs. A neighboring high cello note fragment is visible at lower left.

Opening articulated note and chromatic ascent, complete high sustained-note ties through the middle, both f glyphs of ff, and final low ledger notes/naturals/lower slurs are complete. Neighboring cello arches and note peaks are retained below.

Opening low sustained-note slur, subsequent low sharp notes and both full sf markings including descenders, all high flats/naturals and ties, final low flat/slurred groups and rest match the original. Adjacent cello ink remains below; a previous-system dot remains near the top.
All six whole-bar rests, six measure widths/barlines, clef and three-flat key signature are present. No cello note or marking is assigned to the clarinet rest system.
Three whole-bar rests, fourth-measure rests and p entry, complete high arch and final two sustained notes are preserved. A small neighboring cello-slur fragment is retained at the lower middle.
Opening dotted sustained note and slur, all following alternating upper/lower slurred pairs, full two-measure crescendo wedge, and final sharp sustained note/slur are intact.

Both opening high arches and ledger notes, triplet numeral and arch, lower sharp notes/slurs, full opening f and diminuendo hairpin, central crescendo wedge, rests and final f entry with outgoing slur are complete. Cello slur/note/3 fragments remain below. Source page 4 starts bar 63; the continuing phrase lies beyond this labeled excerpt.

review.notes: Independently rendered and inspected all three original source pages, then chose wider original-source contexts before inspecting recipe rectangles. Compared all 11 source systems with enlarged final output strips and all three complete final pages. Source page 4 confirms the next system starts bar 63. No omitted or clipped target notation was found; all target landmarks listed in Tests/extraction/trio-independent-review.md match. No whiteout exclusions are applied. Six bands retain neighboring/previous-system fragments, permitted by preserve-target; five have no neighboring notation visible. The target staff remains identifiable and readable. Scope is Clarinet in A, bars 1–62, PDF pages 1–3, not the complete trio; the excerpt intentionally ends during a continuing phrase. Original source-page boundaries before bars 22 and 42 are retained; comfortable performance turns are not certified. No transposition or re-engraving is performed, and source notation size remains approximately 97–98%.
